text:
Oliver R.: FYI customer FinServX wants a Private deployment POC. Requirements: no direct internet egress from model hosts, preserve client source IP to backend for audit, and strict firewall allowlist. Can we confirm recommended topology (PrivateLink vs TGW/peering) and a quick pricing delta for Dedicated/reserved vs hosted?
Anna S.: Thanks. Quick Q: are they OK with a customer-managed NAT/proxy for outbound egress to their security stack, or do they want zero egress entirely (i.e., control plane only via PrivateLink)?
Oliver R.: They said zero internet egress from inference nodes. Control plane traffic to Redwood control plane allowed over PrivateLink or a transit path to our control plane endpoints. Need to show exact ports/domains for their firewall team + cost estimate.
Marc P.: For "zero egress" cases we usually recommend Private deployment in their VPC with our software connecting to their onprem proxy, or using AWS PrivateLink interface endpoints to our NLB in a partner VPC. Tradeoffs: PrivateLink gives per-AZ ENIs and is simpler for port-only allowlists. TGW/peering gives more flexible routing but needs transit firewall/NVA for inspection.
Jai N.: Network ops notes: if they want source IP preserved, avoid double NAT. Pattern: (1) Customer VPC <-> TGW attachment -> route to our deployment VPC. Use ENI passthrough or proxy that preserves src-ip (keep client in same net). If using PrivateLink, client traffic originates from customer VPC to an interface endpoint; source IP seen by our side is the endpoint ENI IP (so you lose original client src unless we tunnel over GRE or use X-Forwarded-For at the app layer).
Sarah L.: Security: we'll need a data flow diagram and an answer on KMS/HSM usage + audit logs retention. Also include whether any tokens/traces leave customer VPC and where logs are stored.
Anna S.: For the firewall allowlist, give them minimal port list:

- Control plane (if using PrivateLink): HTTPS 443 to our interface endpoint (private).
- Model serving traffic (internal): TCP 8443 (gRPC) between customer app and inference pool, plus health checks 10256.
- Metrics/monitoring (optional): 9090/9091 to our metrics collector if they want central scraping.

Also asked about FQDN vs IP allowlist — PrivateLink prefers SG+endpoint ENI allowlist (IP). If they require FQDN allowlist for egress, we suggest pointing the proxy at our internal lb FQDN behind PrivateLink.

Sample security group snippet they can paste: 
```
# inbound to inference hosts (from customer app subnet)
Type: TCP
Port: 8443
Source: 10.20.0.0/16  # customer app subnet

# outbound to control plane (via interface endpoint / proxy)
Type: HTTPS
Port: 443
Destination: vpce-0abc123def456  # our PrivateLink endpoint ENI (example)
```

Marc P.: If they want to avoid TLS passthrough and keep X-Forwarded-For, we can deploy a tiny sidecar proxy (envoy) that injects client IP and forwards to model nodes — adds ~50ms, depends on load.
Jai N.: One more caveat: AWS PrivateLink does not preserve original source IP to the service. If preservation is a hard requirement for audit logs, recommend TGW with route-based peering and our service deployed as a VPC attachment (or a customer-managed proxy that forwards src).
Oliver R.: Pricing ask: can you ballpark Dedicated reserved monthly for a small POC (2 mid GPUs, 24/7) and a Private deployment license?
Anna S.: Ballpark: Dedicated (hosted reserved) for 2xA10-equivalent nodes ~ $12k/month (commit pricing incl. infra). Private deployment (customer-managed infra) adds a platform license of ~ $6k/month + support tier. Exacts depend on GPU class and network egress patterns. I put a conservative sticker: $18k/month total for a quick POC estimate.
Sarah L.: Also capture compliance blockers: need to confirm SOC2 scope includes private deploy and whether audit logs are persisted to customer's S3 (preferred). We can offer TLS+KMS integration; clarify HSM requirement if they have FIPS needs.
Oliver R.: Can someone produce a short diagram + allowlist snippet for their firewall team by EOD tomorrow? They want the security answer for SOC/compliance and the cost sheet to sign PO.
Marc P.: I can take diagram and sample rules. Will include both PrivateLink and TGW variants with pros/cons.
Jai N.: I'll validate the SG and route table snippets and give a minimal TGW route example.
Anna S.: I'll update the pricing sheet and add note on license/support.
Sarah L.: I'll write the compliance checklist items (KMS, logs, SOC2, retention) and attach to the questionnaire.
Oliver R.: Great. @Marc P. @Jai N. please ping me when ready; I'll coordinate with FinServX security tomorrow 10am PT. :calendar:
